_readme: Baja SAE page, top to bottom. The timeline on the left is built from the same data.
link: the Longhorn Baja Racing logo in the nav row (Baja page only); opens the team site in a new tab.
overview: the page header and the opening section. roles_detail points are strings, or { title, items } groups.
groups: the two main timeline headings, each with its sections in order.
A section has: id (its #anchor), label (timeline text), title, optional chip (attribution label), optional intro, and blocks.
Block types: points (bullets), goals (numbered goals), specs (label/value rows), table (head + rows), list (short items in columns), text, sub (a subheading), media (images), video.
media items: image (an id from tools/media_map.json), optional caption, optional native: true (never shown larger than the image's own size).

media layouts: grid (same-size 3:4 tiles, up to three per row; a photo of another shape is cropped to fit, and the expanded view shows all of it), row (one line, every image the same height and uncropped; "height": "tile" keeps it no taller than a grid tile), feature, pair, or stack.
Every image opens in an expanded view on click: the 2560 px still where build_media.py made one, else the largest size, with its caption and credit.
A photo's credit comes from tools/media_map.json and shows in the image's bottom-left corner (George Lawrence's competition photos must keep theirs).
Animated images (FEA) play with a Pause button and start paused under reduced motion. The video plays muted while on screen.
Copy is a plain string (from the owner's Baja Page.txt or Baja Draft 2.txt) or { text, draft: true } (drafted during the build; rewrite and drop the flag).
model: the one interactive 3D element. It renders in the section marked model: true once enabled is true and both files exist; nothing 3D loads before that.

overview.label: Overview
overview.title: Longhorn Baja Racing
overview.roles: Founding Member · Vice Captain · Chassis Lead · Manufacturing Lead · Driver
overview.heading: UT Austin Baja SAE – Inaugural Season
overview.intro: In Fall 2025, I joined Longhorn Baja Racing as a founding member, helping bring Baja SAE back to UT Austin for the first time since the 1980s. In our first season, we designed and built a single-seat off-road race car and successfully raced it at Baja SAE Ohio 2026.

stats.text: Led chassis design and fabrication with a team of 5+ engineers, using SolidWorks and ANSYS
Directed manufacturing with 10+ members, turning CAD into race-ready parts for every subsystem
Led sponsor outreach that raised $35,000+ in funding and in-kind support
Helped scale the team from 10 founding members to 175+ students across 11 subteams

sections.label: Chassis CAD Design
sections.title: Chassis CAD Design
sections.intro: Designed in SolidWorks around three first-year goals:

items: Pass Baja SAE technical inspection
Streamlined and simple chassis manufacturing
Flexibility for drivetrain and suspension integration

rows: Passed on the first attempt at competition

sections.label: Tube Selection
sections.title: Tube Selection
sections.intro: Used MATLAB programming to generate a tube size and material analysis for the chassis.

items: Swept tube outer diameter (1.0"–2.5") and wall thickness (0.035"–0.125") across AISI 1018, AISI 4130N, and Docol R8 steel
Computed bending stiffness and bending strength for each combination and compared them to the Baja SAE equivalent minimums
Filtered out every result below the minimums

sections.label: FEA Validation
sections.title: FEA Validation
sections.intro: Static structural FEA in ANSYS on the chassis under front impact, side impact, and front rollover load cases. The same analysis validated the front bulkhead geometry and confirmed that the rear packaging and engine mount tubes could carry the full powertrain loads.

items.caption: Front collision, tow hook only · 10,000 lbf
Side & Frontal Impact · 10,000 lbf frontal + 5,000 lbf side
